questions: Does oval steering_oscillation fall below about 0.2 from 0.309 with the restored inertia?
Does oval progress hold near 0.4, or does the heavier robot lose speed?
Does max_error move below 0.06 m, or does it stay at 0.062 m? If it stays, is the reaction point now the limit?
Is there any line loss on the slalom at the outer sensors?

intent: Test whether yaw inertia, not track width, sets the steering oscillation. Restore mass 0.8 kg and body_length 0.16 m (inertia back to the iteration 1 value of about 0.0027) while keeping the 0.10 m track that gave the best oval progress. Sensing and wheel radius are unchanged, so any change in oscillation comes from inertia.
learning: Iteration 3 falsified the prediction that a wider track lowers oscillation (0.272 to 0.309 as width went 0.09 to 0.10 m). Track width and yaw inertia were confounded across iterations 1 to 3, and inertia now looks like the stronger candidate. Next, test inertia alone. If oscillation tracks inertia, mass and body length are the damping levers. If it does not, the controller gain is the remaining cause, and geometry should stop chasing oscillation.
rationale:
Iteration 3 (0.10 m track) did not help. Oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.309, up from 0.272 at 0.09 m, so the Integrator's rule to widen the track further is not supported. Oval progress held at 0.45, and line loss stayed at 0 on the oval and s-bend, with 0.25 events per run on the slalom. Max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064 m on every track, so every run still leaves the 0.06 m off-track floor. Body width cannot raise that floor (it would need body_width above 0.19 m), so tracking must improve.

Across iterations, oscillation does not follow track width alone. Iteration 1 (0.12 m track, 0.8 kg, 0.16 m body) gave the lowest oscillation, 0.173. Iterations 2 and 3 (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body) gave 0.272 and 0.309. Yaw inertia, mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, is 0.00267 in iteration 1 and 0.00144 in iterations 2 and 3, roughly halved. The most consistent explanation is that the lighter, shorter robot is less damped and twitches more. Track width and inertia were changed together in iteration 1 to 2, so this is not proven.

Decision: keep the 0.10 m track, which gave the best oval progress (0.45), and restore the iteration 1 inertia by returning mass to 0.8 kg and body_length to 0.16 m. Sensors, wheel radius and body width stay fixed, so the change isolates inertia. Expected result: oval oscillation falls toward 0.17 to 0.2, progress stays near 0.35 to 0.45, and max_error is unchanged near 0.062 m. If oscillation falls but progress drops below about 0.35, the next lever is wheel_radius 0.035 m. If max_error still sits at 0.062 m, the reaction point (sensor y) is the limit, and I will test y = 0.02 m next.
